who: Guy Howard Miller (G. Howard Miller), historian at the University of Texas at Austin; PhD Michigan 1970.

evidence.says: Guy Howard Miller's CV lists a Michigan PhD in 1970 and faculty appointments at UT Austin beginning in 1971.
Penne Restad's O Holy Night: The Creation of an American Christmas is listed under 1994, supervised by G. Howard Miller.
The G. H. Miller authority identifies Gerson Harry Miller, an Edinboro professor with a 1957 USC PhD in educational psychology.
The Guy Miller authority identifies a Palo Alto historian and newspaper librarian associated with Stanford's class of 1901.
The Guy W. Miller authority is established from Agricultural marketing in Pakistan (1958), credited to Guy W. Miller, M.A.

notes: The supervisor is Guy Howard Miller, not the supplied Gerson Harry Miller, Guy W. Miller, or Palo Alto Guy Miller. No supplied candidate identifies G. Howard Miller; the automated Michigan agreement is misleading. UT lists Restad in 1994 rather than the AHA's 1993.

who: Silvia Z. Mitchell, historian of early modern Europe and Spain at Purdue; PhD Miami 2013.

evidence.says: Her CV lists a Miami history PhD in May 2013, Purdue appointments since August 2013, and doctoral supervision of Caroline Fish's Spanish diplomacy dissertation in progress.
The authority for Silvia Z. Mitchell cites Queen, mother, and stateswoman (2019) and identifies her as Purdue's assistant professor of early modern European history.

notes: Full name, department, field, doctorate and named doctoral student agree; the 2023 CV uses an earlier dissertation title.

who: Georgina M. Montgomery, historian of science at Michigan State; PhD Minnesota 2005.

evidence.says: MSU's faculty biography gives her Minnesota history of science and technology PhD in 2005 and appointment to Lyman Briggs and History in fall 2008.
The graduate committee list records A. Lewis's 2015 history PhD, Amboseli landscapes, with G. Montgomery as advisor.
The Georgina M. Montgomery authority cites Primates in the real world (2015) and identifies an assistant professor of history at Michigan State.

notes: The authority's middle initial, institutional career and field fit the supervisor; the student and doctorate are independently corroborated.

who: John M. Nieto-Phillips, historian of US Latino history at Indiana University Bloomington; history PhD UCLA.

evidence.says: Indiana lists John Nieto-Phillips as associate professor of history, with campus leadership roles spanning 2016–2022 and authorship of The Language of Blood.
UCLA identifies the Indiana history and Latino studies professor and author of The Language of Blood as holding BA, MA and PhD degrees in history from UCLA.
The John M. Nieto-Phillips authority cites The language of blood (2004) and identifies its author as a professor of history and Latino studies at Indiana University.

notes: Same book, institution, field and doctoral institution; the documented Indiana career covers the student's 2020 doctorate.

who: Thomas Schaub Noonan, historian of medieval Russia at Minnesota; PhD Indiana 1965.

evidence.says: REEIfication (October 2001), pp. 11–12, commemorates Thomas Schaub Noonan, a medieval Russian historian who joined Minnesota's history department in 1966, a year after his doctorate.
The alumni obituary states that Noonan received his Indiana PhD in 1965 and was a Minnesota professor from 1966.
The authority identifies Thomas S. (Thomas Schaub) Noonan as a Minnesota history professor educated at Indiana, and cites his 1965 Dnieper trade-route dissertation.

notes: Full name, medieval Russian specialization, Minnesota career and Indiana doctorate distinguish this candidate from the other Noonans.

who: Adriana Novoa, historian of Latin America and science at South Florida; PhD UC San Diego 1998.

evidence.says: USF lists Novoa as a history professor with a 1998 UC San Diego PhD and research on science in Latin America, including From Man to Ape.
Jason R. Old's 2023 history dissertation, The Politics of Waves, names Adriana Novoa as major professor.
The authority cites From man to ape and USF's history faculty page, identifying Adriana Novoa at South Florida with the same research specialization.

notes: Direct student supervision, exact doctorate and the authority's institutional and publication evidence agree.

who: Deanne Love Stephens, also published as Deanne Nuwer, historian at Southern Mississippi; PhD there in 1996.

evidence.says: USM lists Deanne Stephens as professor of history and Gulf South center co-director, with an institutional account under Deanne Nuwer.
John J. Mangipano's 2017 history dissertation on William Walker and progressive imperialism lists Deanne Nuwer as committee chair.
The catalogue records Deanne Love Stephens Nuwer's The 1878 yellow fever epidemic in Mississippi as a Southern Mississippi PhD dissertation, 1996.
The Deanne Love Stephens authority cites The Mississippi Gulf Coast seafood industry (2021), whose author biography identifies a Southern Mississippi history professor.

notes: University and dissertation records connect the Stephens and Nuwer name forms and confirm the named student's supervision.

who: Frederic Austin Ogg, historian and political scientist at Wisconsin; history PhD Harvard 1908.

evidence.says: Wisconsin's account identifies Frederic Austin Ogg as a faculty member from 1914 for 34 years, and political science department chair from 1925 to 1939.
The biography records his Harvard history PhD in 1908 and Wisconsin appointment beginning in 1914.
The Frederic Austin Ogg authority cites Jay's treaty and a 1919 work identifying its author as a Wisconsin professor with a doctorate.

notes: Full name, Wisconsin appointment covering 1925, and Harvard doctorate agree; the political science department label does not indicate a different person.
